topics.label: Introduction to cancer biology and the lecture’s aims
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes students, frames the lecture series, and sets out the learning outcomes rather than teaching the lecture’s substantive subject.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic changes in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how genetic, epigenetic, and infection-related changes accumulate during cancer development and raises questions about that process.

topics.label: Cancer as a failure of differentiation and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These ideas describe cancer as a breakdown of normal cellular roles and tissue organization that can lead to invasion.

topics.label: Cell culture models of cancer and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic considers what studying tumor cells in culture can reveal and what is lost when cells are separated from the tumor’s wider structure.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, malignancy, and benign-tumor behavior
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how tumor behavior is classified along the transition from contained growth to invasion and possible metastasis, while clarifying what benign tumors can and cannot do.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature by tissue of origin and malignancy
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic sets out the naming conventions used to distinguish tumor types and their malignant status.

topics.label: How cancer causes illness and death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumors impair normal bodily functions and how primary and secondary tumors can lead to death.

topics.label: Patterns of tumor incidence across humans and other animals
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how tumor types and their frequency vary across human populations and animal species.

topics.label: Clinical presentation and cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why cancer can be difficult to detect and compare screening approaches for finding it earlier.

topics.label: Lecture close and revision guidance
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by directing students to review the learning outcomes and indicating what comes next.
